item.title: America’s Labor Market Is Paralyzed by Policy and Economic Uncertainty
item.description: In markets, options to buy and sell securities get more valuable when volatility increases. The same is true of employers making hiring and firing decisions in times of surging input costs like energy prices, chaotic trade policies and transformative technologies. When you can’t predict next quarter’s bottom line, you’re better off retaining optionality, delaying staffing decisions that can involve steep up-front costs and are difficult to reverse. item.dc:creator: Jonathan Levin

item.title: Can China’s Shanghai Cooperation Organization Become the New NATO?
item.description: Washington wants the world to get with its program, but much of the world has moved on.
item.dc:creator: Howard Chua-Eoan

item.title: The Tech Mogul Strongman Is On the Rise
item.description: The rise of the liberal order in the 19th century depended on two revolutions. The most obvious was in the political sphere, where reformers restrained over-mighty rulers with a combination of constitutional rules and individual rights. But just as important was the transformation of the business world that created public companies, answerable to their shareowners rather than the government.
item.dc:creator: Adrian Wooldridge

item.title: ‘The Salt Path’ Film Is a Lesson in What We Want to Believe
item.description: Arriving in theaters nationwide Friday: The Salt Path, based on Raynor Winn’s bestselling memoir of the same title. The film stars Gillian Anderson and Jason Isaacs as a British couple who, suddenly homeless and facing a dire medical diagnosis, take a life-changing hike along the dramatic Cornish coast.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Green Carmichael

item.title: Altman's Opaque AI Is Creating a New Security Dilemma
item.description: Artificial-intelligence researchers have spent the last year toying with a compelling proposition: AI models could be more powerful and cheaper to run if they disclosed less about how they worked. The trade-off is risky, as it could become harder for humans to check the systems aren’t doing anything harmful. But it would also provide a commercial advantage.
item.dc:creator: Parmy Olson

item.title: Grocery Prices Are a Real Problem for Voters. Do Politicians Actually Care?
item.description: Food prices play an outsized role in how Americans view affordability. When you’re bombarded with bigger price tags and shrinking product sizes on every trip to the grocery store, it’s an in-your-face reminder that we’re losing purchasing power. It’s leading to widespread anxiety. According to an Associated Press-NORC poll released in August, 41% of Americans say they are concerned about being able to afford groceries, up from 24% in April.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ellen Klas

item.title: ICE and Immigration Enforcement Are Less Visible, More Damaging
item.description: It’s ironic that Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has so often found himself at odds with the immigration hardliners who are among President Donald Trump’s most loyal supporters. Just last month, Mullin (correctly) acknowledged there’s a difference between immigrants seeking legal status and those flouting the law, and then — sin of all apparent sins — advocated for employment visas to address labor shortages.
item.dc:creator: Erika D. Smith

item.title: Measles Outbreak Puts CDC’s Erica Schwartz to Her First Test
item.description: A tragedy in Pennsylvania — two measles-related deaths, including that of an infant — has devolved into a political circus led by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Jarvis

item.title: Hegseth Is Gutting the Army Amid War With Iran
item.description: The sudden departure of Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll, following months of tension with Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, is a serious blow to American security. Worse, his resignation follows the forcing out of several top Army generals, including Chief of Staff Randy George, Vice Chief James Mingus and the highly regarded combat commander of US Army Europe, Chris Donahue.
item.dc:creator: James Stavridis

item.title: German Notary Reading Marathons Are Pushing Tech Entrepreneurs to Despair
item.description: Germany is proud of its legal quirks, rightly so at times. No Sunday shopping, no jaywalking and no speed limits on the Autobahn all have reasonable justifications.
item.dc:creator: Chris Bryant

item.title: Putin’s Shadow War Against Europe Is Getting More Intense
item.description: Grueling wars are now the global norm. For years, a brutal conflict has consumed Ukraine. For months, a grinding faceoff has convulsed the Persian Gulf. Now Russia is escalating a different kind of fight: a shadow war of violent, quasi-covert coercion against Europe. The continent, once a paragon of post-Cold War peace, faces a dangerous struggle, just as ambiguous signals from Washington make Moscow harder to deter.
item.dc:creator: Hal Brands

item.title: Zack Polanski MP: Can Andy Burnham Slay the Eco-Socialist Dragon, Too?
item.description: Andy Burnham won power in Britain this summer by proving to his own Labour Party that he could beat the hard-right populists of Reform UK. Now, thanks to a flounce out of Parliament by the prime minister he usurped, he has a chance to show he can slay dragons on the left too.
item.dc:creator: Rosa Prince
